evidence.quote: This Directive establishes a common framework of measures to promote energy efficiency within the Union

summary.short: Recast EU energy efficiency directive setting a framework for energy efficiency targets, the energy efficiency first principle, public-sector energy savings, energy savings obligations, energy audits, energy management systems and data-centre reporting. Binding on Member States, which must transpose it. Adopted 13 September 2023.
summary.long: Directive (EU) 2023/1791 recasts Directive 2012/27/EU and establishes a common Union framework to promote energy efficiency and meet Union energy efficiency targets. Member States must apply an energy efficiency first principle in planning, policy and major investment decisions above EUR 100 million (EUR 175 million for transport infrastructure) (Art. 3). Member States must collectively reduce final energy consumption by at least 11.7% in 2030 compared with the 2020 EU Reference Scenario and set indicative national contributions (Art. 4). Public bodies must reduce their final energy consumption by at least 1.9% each year (Art. 5), renovate at least 3% of the floor area of publicly owned buildings each year (Art. 6), and purchase high energy-efficiency products and services (Art. 7). Member States must achieve cumulative end-use energy savings through obligation schemes or alternative policy measures, with designated obligated parties (Arts 8 to 10). Enterprises above set annual energy consumption must implement a certified energy management system or undergo energy audits (Art. 11). Owners and operators of data centres with at least 500 kW of installed IT power must make energy performance information publicly available, and the Commission maintains a European database (Art. 12). Articles 13 and 14 set metering requirements for natural gas and for heating, cooling and domestic hot water. The document provided ends with Article 14; later provisions are not included in this file.

Obligations, thresholds, events, enforcement and definitions were not requested for this run and are not coded. Target instrument IDs are empty strings because no registry IDs were supplied; target_text identifies each target. Obligated parties (Art. 9(3)), data centre owners and operators (Art. 12(1)) and enterprises (Art. 11) are categories and are not coded as named entities. Two operative data-centre thresholds differ: 500 kW installed IT power for the reporting duty (Art. 12(1)) and 1 MW for the best-practice encouragement (Art. 12(4)); both are left for the thresholds pass. Recital (155) limits transposition to substantive amendments, so unchanged provisions remain under Directive 2012/27/EU. Part 2 of 2 (Articles 15 to 40 and Annexes I to XVII). Relations and entities are drawn only from this part. target_instrument_id is empty because registry IDs for the targets were not supplied. Annex I and Annex II formulas are not reproduced in the text. Article 36(1) does not list Articles 13 to 20 in its transposition list, although Article 39 makes them apply from 12 October 2025. Annex XVI Part A lists earlier acts that amended Directive 2012/27/EU; these are not coded here as relations of this Directive.
